description: Command injection in spawn-worker! via session-id. The session-id is extracted from filenames in the requests directory without sanitization and then passed directly into a shell command via format and system.
code_snippet:
(define (spawn-worker! session-id)
  (let* ([scheme (scheme-command)]
         [script *worker-script*]
         [log (log-path session-id)]
         [cmd (if (windows?)
                  (format "cmd.exe /c start /b \"\" \"~a\" --script ~a ~a"
                          scheme script session-id)
                  (format "~a --script ~a ~a > ~a 2>&1 &"
                          scheme script session-id log))])
        ... (system cmd)))
suggested_fix: Sanitize the session-id to ensure it only contains alphanumeric characters or use a safer process spawning mechanism that doesn't involve a shell string.

description: Path traversal and arbitrary file write in identity-head-path. The username symbol is converted to a string and appended to the heads directory path without checking for directory traversal sequences (e.g., ../).
suggested_fix: Validate that the username symbol does not contain directory traversal characters like '/' or '..', or use a hash of the username for the filename.

description: Command injection in terminate-worker! via pid. The pid is read from a file and passed to a shell command without verification that it is indeed a numeric value.
code_snippet:
(define (terminate-worker! session-id)
  (let ([pid (read-number-file (pid-path session-id))])
       (when pid
             (if (windows?)
                 (system (format "taskkill /PID ~a /F >nul 2>nul" pid))
                 (begin
                  (system (format "kill ~a 2>/dev/null" pid))
                  (when (process-alive? pid)
                        (system (format "kill -9 ~a 2>/dev/null" pid))))))))
suggested_fix: Ensure that the value read from the pid file is a number before passing it to system, or use a native Scheme interface to send signals to processes.

description: Path traversal in session-id extraction. extract-session-id-from-filename does not prevent directory traversal if the directory-list returns malicious filenames containing '..'.
code_snippet:
(define (extract-session-id-from-filename filename)
  (let ([len (string-length filename)])
       (if (and (>= len 3) (string=? (substring filename (- len 3) len) ".ss"))
           (substring filename 0 (- len 3))
           filename)))
suggested_fix: Add a check to ensure the filename does not contain path separators or '..' before using it as a session-id.

description: Potential Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) via user-provided regex patterns in tag-matches and payload-matches.
suggested_fix: Implement a timeout for regex matching or restrict the complexity of allowed regular expressions.
